Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http Ilwww. dil .gov.ph OPINION NO. -Ld- OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY 25 JUL OFFICE OF THE SANGGUNIANG BAYAN Municipality of Busuanga Province of Palawan Attention: MR. BENJAMIN A. RODRIGUEZ Chairman, Committee on Finance, Appropriation & Taxation Dear Mr. Rodriguez: This refers to your letter dated 13 March 2017 seeking this Department's legal opinion on the legality of the status of a Barangay Kagawad who was appointed as a Fish Warden for a Marine Protected Area in the same barangay, under the Office of the Municipal Agriculture, by the Municipal Mayor. Based on your letter, Mayor Elizabeth M. Cervantes of Busuanga, Palawan appointed Brgy. Kagawad Arnilo Abreu of Barangay Concepcion to be the Fish Warden for a Marine Protected Area in Brgy. Concepcion. Hence, this present request for a legal opinion. This Department agrees with your stand. Section 94 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" provides: "Section 94. xxx No elective or appointive local official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. xxx" In DILG Legal Opinion No. 24, s. 2004, issued on 17 February 2004, this Department addressed the issue on the employment of the punong barangay, barangay kagawads, SK Chairman, barangay secretary and barangay treasurer in public and private establishments, offices and other businesses. The said DILG Legal Opinion states that: "xxx Let it be cleared, however, that they cannot hold other public offices in view of the express prohibition under Section 94 of s, 202

the Local Government Code which provides that 'no elective or appointive local official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure'. Furthermore, it provides that 'unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no elective or appointive local official shall hold any other office or employment in the Government or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof, including government-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries. ' Accordingly, we can thus conclude that elective and appointive officials are prohibited and not eligible to be appointed or even designated in any capacity to any public office or employment in the Government unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of their positions. xxx" This Department, likewise, in DILG Legal Opinion No. 72, s. 2004 (August 23, 2004), ruled upon the issue on whether or not the City Mayor can appoint an incumbent Punong Barangay as Chief of the Solid Waste Management Office. This Department declared: "xxx, Section 94 of the Local Government Code squarely addresses the matter. Section 94 provides: 'Section 94. xxx No elective or appointive local official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. xxx' It is clear from said provision of law that an elective local official cannot be employed in any government position which requires appointment or designation. Thus, the incumbent Punong Barangay, being an elective local official, cannot be appointed as Chief of Solid Waste Management Office, a position in the government service. " Going back to the present issue, Mayor Cervantes cannot, therefore, appoint Kagawad Abreu to be the Fish Warden for a Marine Protected Area, a position in the government service without violating the provision of the Local Government Code. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. uly yo rs, Legal: 24 A STERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary for Local Governme • OUSIG -21-0 201
